title: Page-mode immersive header overlaps the first body line
symptom: On a Pixel 8 / Android 14 emulator in page mode, the lightweight immersive header could collide with the first visible body line. A real imported TXT showed the header bottom at y=253 while the first body line started at y=248 before the fix.
root_cause: Page mode used a 44dp base top padding for page text. That converted to a text top that sat above the measured bottom of the immersive header on the current device, while scroll mode already reserved a larger 52dp top band. During the 2026-09-20 visual revision, expanding the back target to 48dp while retaining a 14dp top offset recreated overlap in the touch region: its bottom reached 62dp even though the body still started at 52dp.
fix: Raised the page-mode base top padding from 44dp to 52dp so the first page line clears the immersive header band.
Added an instrumented regression that compares the visible bounds of the immersive header and first body text.
Verified the same real TXT after the fix: the header bottom remained y=253 and the first body line moved to y=269, leaving visible separation.

The 2026-09-20 revision keeps the 48dp back target but starts it at 4dp. It does not change the 52dp body inset or repaginate on chrome changes. ReaderTtsControlsTest.continuationTextTouchDoesNotTriggerTheImmersiveBackButton first reproduced an unexpected back callback at (20dp,55dp), then passed with no back callback after the correction.
failed_attempts: Do not rely on static padding values unless they are checked against the actual header bounds on the target device.
Avoid deriving page top padding from the temporary chrome-visible top bar; that can repaginate content when the chrome appears or hides.
impact: Keeps the first page readable in the default page-mode reader and prevents the persistent immersive header from visually pressing into real novel text.

follow_up_2026_10_16.observation: The related device suite reported header=Rect(37,143-347,269) and body=Rect(63,269-440,338). The header's 48dp touch region ended at y=269px and the first body text line box started at y=269px: their edges met without a positive-area overlap. Inspection of the actual screen confirmed that the first body line was complete.
follow_up_2026_10_16.test_correction: ReaderChromeTest.persistentHeaderShowsBackAndCurrentChapterWithoutRevealingChrome still required header.bottom + 8 <= body.top. That extra 8px gap was an outdated assertion after the 2026-09-20 change to a 4dp top offset plus a 48dp back target. The test now requires header.bottom <= body.top, matching non-overlap of the touch region and body line box. This does not add top padding, move the body or alter pagination; these node bounds are not the visible glyph outlines.

verification.screen_and_existing_touch_regression: The actual screen showed a complete first line, and the existing ReaderTtsControlsTest.continuationTextTouchDoesNotTriggerTheImmersiveBackButton regression passed. This supports preserving the first-line reading gesture outside the back target.
verification.updated_directed_test: Confirmed GREEN on StoryReader_API34 on 2026-10-16 after correcting the assertion. The direct case passed without changing header or body layout.
